== Biography ==

Mr. McGregor is a farmer who owns and maintains a garden planted with lettuces, French beans, radishes, and parsley. His property is notorious among the local rabbit families as a place of great peril, and mothers warn their children away from it with stories of past misfortune.

The most grim of these tales concerns Peter's own father, who entered the garden years ago and met with an accident. The incident ended tragically, as he was subsequently made into a pie by Mrs. McGregor—a fate that lends weight to the maternal warnings and establishes Mr. McGregor's garden as a place where trespassers face grave consequences.

The young rabbit Peter, despite these warnings, could not resist the temptation of the garden. He squeezed under the gate and ate some of the lettuces and French beans, followed by radishes. After feeling rather sick from his meal, he ventured deeper into the garden in search of parsley.

== Personality ==

Mr. McGregor is the owner of a substantial garden and a man of decided will. He maintains strict prohibitions against trespass and does not tolerate intrusion into his domain, making his expectations abundantly clear to all who might venture near.

When Peter breaches his garden, McGregor's response is immediate and forceful. He seizes a rake and pursues the young rabbit, calling out 'Stop thief!' across the grounds. His pursuit is determined and vigorous, leaving no doubt as to his commitment to defending his property.

This forceful defense of his property reveals McGregor as a man of uncompromising principle. He permits no exception to his rule, regardless of who the offender may be. His commitment to defending his garden is absolute.

The consequences of trespass in McGregor's garden are not mere warnings but established facts, backed by his demonstrated willingness to act forcefully against any breach of his boundaries.
